title: 15-Minute Lemon Herb Butter Shrimp Skillet (One Pan!)
description: Make this 15-minute lemon herb butter shrimp skillet in a single pan for a fast, no-fuss weeknight dinner loaded with garlic and citrus flavor.
story: By the time I lugged my groceries up three flights of stairs in my tiny apartment, it was already past 7:30 PM. The absolute last thing on my radar was scrubbing a mountain of dishes. I just wanted something that tasted like I actually tried, minus the sink chaos. I grabbed a bag of frozen shrimp from Trader Joe's, a couple of lemons rolling around my crisper drawer, and a stick of Kerrygold butter. The first time I tested this, I cranked the skillet way too high and burned the garlic into bitter charcoal—total rookie mistake. Once I dialed the heat down to medium-low, everything clicked. This lemon herb butter shrimp skillet comes together in one single pan, takes barely fifteen minutes, and keeps my sink practically empty. Total weeknight survival mode, accomplished.
ingredients: 1.5 lbs large shrimp, peeled, deveined, and patted completely dry with paper towels
1/3 cup low-sodium chicken broth or dry white wine
1/2 teaspoon kosher salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
1 crusty loaf of French bread or Trader Joe's brioche for serving
instructions: Step 1: Pat your shrimp as dry as you possibly can with paper towels. Seriously, wet shrimp steams instead of searing, and we want that golden color. Season with kosher salt and black pepper.

Step 2: Heat your avocado oil and 1 tablespoon of butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Lay the shrimp in a single layer without crowding them. Let them sear for 2 minutes on the first side until pink.

Step 3: Flip the shrimp, toss in the minced garlic, and cook for just 1 more minute. The garlic should smell incredible, not burnt. Immediately pull the shrimp out of the skillet and transfer them to a plate so they don't turn rubbery.

Step 4: Turn the heat down to low. Pour in the chicken broth, fresh lemon juice, and lemon zest, scraping up any delicious browned bits stuck to the bottom of the pan. Whisk in the remaining 3 tablespoons of butter until melted and glossy. Toss the shrimp back in for 30 seconds to warm through, sprinkle with fresh parsley, and serve immediately with plenty of crusty bread.
proHack: Don't walk away from the stove when the garlic goes in! Garlic burns in seconds and turns bitter. Add it during the last minute of cooking the shrimp, and immediately pull the pan off the heat if it starts to brown too fast.
storage: Store any leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. To reheat, skip the microwave (unless you want rubbery shrimp) and toss them into a warm skillet over low heat for just 2 minutes until warm.

faqs.question: Can I substitute chicken broth if I don't have it?
faqs.answer: Totally. You can use dry white wine for a brighter zip, or simply use pasta water if you decide to serve this over noodles.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the shrimp from getting rubbery?
faqs.answer: Shrimp cooks insanely fast. As soon as they curl into a 'C' shape and turn pink, get them off the direct heat. They will keep cooking slightly in the pan.
